_doc: Canonical spelling for prose (SCHEMES[].desc + every narration string).
Two rules settled with the author on 2026-07-25, and they are not the upstream ones:
1. Where a term already had a dominant form in the catalog, that form wins. So Kubelet, ETCD
and Node-1 keep their capitals even though kubernetes.io writes kubelet, etcd and node-1.
The exception is the hyphenated command names, where the catalog was already lowercase
and unanimous (kube-proxy 59/59), so they stay lowercase.
2. Node, Pod and Service are ALWAYS capitalized, including in ordinary phrasing like
'both Pods land on the same Node'. This one overrides the count: node ran 220 to 184.
Three classes, and the difference decides what the linter says about a sentence opening:
hard-capital  one correct form, capitalized. Opening a sentence with it is fine.
hard-lower    a NAME that must never be capitalized (kubectl, kube-proxy). Opening a
sentence with it collides with the capital rule, so the linter says REWORD.
soft          also an ordinary English noun (a container, the controller), so the linter
reports the distribution and a human judges. Sentence-initial case is ignored.
Inline diagram strings (label / name / wire) are NOT scanned here: that is B7.
TRAP: a fully qualified name written with its trailing dot (api.ns.svc.cluster.local.) looks
exactly like a sentence end, so anything lowercase after it is reported as a sentence opening
lowercase. Put a comma straight after the dot, or end the sentence on the name. Do not widen the
splitter for it: telling a real lowercase opening from a false one is the whole job of that rule.

hard.Kubelet: component name, capitalized here by decision (catalog majority 130 to 57)
hard.ETCD: capitalized here by decision (catalog majority 25 to 6)
hard.Node: ALWAYS capitalized by decision, including ordinary phrasing
hard.Node-1: node name, capitalized by decision (catalog majority 63 to 27)
hard.Node-2: node name, capitalized by decision (catalog majority 26 to 15)
hard.Node-3: node name, capitalized by decision (catalog majority 2 to 1)
hard.Node-a: node name, capitalized like its numbered siblings
hard.Node-b: node name, capitalized like its numbered siblings

hardLower.kubectl: ALWAYS lowercase by decision, as a tool mention and as a command line alike. Most prose occurrences are copy-pasteable commands (kubectl apply -f, kubectl drain), where a capital would make the command invalid. Kubelet is the opposite by the same decision: see hard.
hardLower.kube-apiserver: binary name, lowercase like its siblings
hardLower.kube-scheduler: binary name, lowercase in prose. On the diagram the box is labelled Scheduler on all six cards that draw it, which is the catalog form for a component heading, like Kubelet
hardLower.cloud-controller-manager: binary name, lowercase like its siblings

_exceptionsDoc: Contexts where a term is a LITERAL and its casing is not ours to correct. Measured, not
guessed: on the DNS unit the linter was wrong 10 times out of 15 without these, which is the
rate at which a rule stops being a rule and becomes a report. Each pattern is a regex matched
against the whole string, and a hit inside its range is skipped.
Add one only after checking every occurrence of the term catalog-wide, or the exception hides
real defects. `pod CIDR` for instance is the standing lowercase term (the podCIDR field), while
`a new pod lands in etcd` two cards away is a genuine miss that must keep failing.

soft.Job: ordinary noun far more often than the API kind: all 10 lowercase hits are English (its entire job, does one job) or part of a kubectl command
soft.Ingress: the API kind and the plain word for inbound traffic (ingress bandwidth, split ingress across teams) are both in use, so this one is judged per sentence
soft.Container: ordinary noun in this catalog (container 265 to 1), not an API kind
soft.Volume: ordinary noun in this catalog (volume 169, unanimous), not an API kind
soft.Namespace: ordinary noun in this catalog (namespace 56, unanimous)
soft.Controller: generic role (controller 119 to 2), capitalize only inside a proper name
soft.Scheduler: generic role (scheduler 32 to 18), capitalize only when it names kube-scheduler
soft.Endpoints: plain plural far more often than the API kind (endpoints 14 to 2)

inlineDoc: B7, system A: a BLOCK LABEL is a heading and takes a capital, everything else on the canvas
(sublabel, chip name, chip value, wire label) is body text and stays lowercase.
Only the FIRST TOKEN decides, because the rule is about the first character. A string opening
with an identifier, an acronym, a gRPC method or a published API word is untouchable: Pod IP,
CRI gRPC, RunPodSandbox, Waiting, ReadWriteOnce, POST /api/v1/pods.
`names` is the same idea as hardLower for prose: a plain lowercase word that is really a NAME.
app alone is 59 labels and is the container name, so capitalizing it would be a defect.
`components` is the other half of B7, and casing rules cannot express it: it is about whether
the NAME is right at all. Api, Kubectl and ControllerManager all passed the casing rule for
23 cards because they open with a capital. Only a dictionary of real component names sees them.
It holds names that are objectively WRONG (a missing hyphen, a Title-cased acronym), never
names that are merely inconsistent with the rest of the catalog: Kube-apiserver against API x22
and Conntrack against conntrack are both legitimate spellings, so they belong to a human
review, where someone picks the winner. Mixing the two classes is what makes a rule unenforceable.

_apiWordsDoc: A first token whose casing belongs to Kubernetes, Linux or a protocol rather than to this
project, so system A leaves the string alone. Most are ordinary English words that are also
legal API enum values: filesystem and block for volumeMode, retain and delete for the reclaim
policy, true and false for a condition status.
memory: the value Memory, the only NON-EMPTY legal value of emptyDir.medium, drawn on the
medium chip of storage-emptydir. That one string is all this entry exempts today, and the
empty medium is drawn as node disk on the same chip, so the chip is not a pure literal.
KNOWN LIMITATION of the whole list, not of any one entry: untouchable() in render/inline.test.mjs
short-circuits BEFORE the want check, so an entry exempts want title as well as want lower.
A future BLOCK LABEL whose first token matches any word here will never be told to take its
capital. Weigh that before adding one, and prefer a token isIdentifier already accepts.
_homographsDoc: Two spellings that are two different objects, so no term rule may merge them.
Each earns its line by evidence, never by convenience: an entry here hides a real defect.
forward: the CoreDNS forward plugin block, against the netfilter FORWARD chain.
podb: Pod B is the generic second Pod on five cards, pod-b is a Pod that
storage-ephemeral-storage-eviction names in its narration next to pod-c.
apinssvcclusterlocal: the trailing dot is the whole subject of the last step of
network-dns-ndots. api.ns.svc.cluster.local is a relative name the resolver builds
from the search list, api.ns.svc.cluster.local. is absolute and skips that list, so
the two spellings name two different lookups and must not be merged.
